question: A point source $S$ emits monochromatic light in a uniform transparent medium. At $t=0$, the source is switched on. At a later time $t$, the disturbance has travelled the same distance in all directions (treat the medium as isotropic). (a) Create a neat labeled diagram in the $xy$-plane showing the wavefronts at times $t$, $2t$ and $3t$. (b) A small rectangular region inside the medium has refractive index $n_2$ (with $n_2>n_1$ of the surrounding medium). A plane wavefront is incident normally on this region, and the wavefront enters the region simultaneously across its entire height. Neglect diffraction near the boundary. Create the emergent wavefront immediately after it leaves the region and write the expression for the time delay $\Delta \tau$ introduced between the part of the wavefront that passed through $n_2$ and the part that remained in $n_1$ (region thickness $t_0$).

options.A: At times $t,2t,3t$ the wavefronts are ellipses; and $\Delta\tau=\dfrac{(n_2-n_1)t_0}{2c}$.
options.B: At times $t,2t,3t$ the wavefronts are concentric circles; and $\Delta\tau=\dfrac{(n_2-n_1)t_0}{c}$.
options.C: At times $t,2t,3t$ the wavefronts are concentric circles; and $\Delta\tau=\dfrac{(n_2+n_1)t_0}{c}$.
options.D: At times $t,2t,3t$ the wavefronts are straight parallel lines; and $\Delta\tau=\dfrac{(n_2-n_1)c}{t_0}$.
